scenes.display_title: Raised beds and bunk-bed design review
scenes.spoken_text: Elevated and bunk beds need specialist verification of falls, entrapment, support and access. Prepare a traceable review record; the figures are hazard maps, not construction drawings.
scenes.caption: Elevated and bunk beds need specialist verification of falls, entrapment, support and access. Prepare a traceable review record; the figures are hazard maps, not construction drawings.

scenes.display_title: Identify the product, user and market
scenes.spoken_text: Identify the product definition, intended user and market. US reference 16 CFR 1513 addresses elevated children’s beds within its scope and requires the warning against upper-bunk use below age 6. Reaching 6 does not itself establish suitability. Verify current requirements for the intended market and product; the absence of a lower bed does not automatically exclude a loft bed from review.
scenes.caption: Classify first; a US reference does not replace local applicability review.

scenes.display_title: Review guards, mattress and openings as a system
scenes.spoken_text: Mark guards relative to the specified mattress, end openings, wall interfaces, ladder route and supports. A thicker mattress changes the exposed guard height; do not improvise an added rail. Entrapment assessment depends on opening shape, location and defined test methods, not one general gap rule. Never use a child’s head or body as a test probe.
scenes.caption: Review the mattress, guards and openings together; a sketch is not a test result.

scenes.spoken_text: Link applicable requirement, drawing revision, product/mattress identity, verifier, result and outstanding action. CPSC guidance explains accepted third-party testing, children’s product certification and additional US requirements; establish what applies in the project’s market. Obtain assembly, labeling and service instructions. A visual prototype or one adult standing on a bed is not a substitute for required system testing.
scenes.caption: Requirement + identified configuration + traceable result.

scenes.spoken_text: The exercise proposes an upper bunk for a 4-year-old and provides only an unidentified image. Reject that allocation and review an appropriate non-elevated sleeping alternative with product verification. Even changing the user’s age would not resolve the separate absence of system evidence. Decision: reject the upper-bunk allocation and obtain evidence for a suitable alternative.
scenes.caption: Decision: reject the upper-bunk allocation and obtain evidence for a suitable alternative.
